items.text: Algebraic geometry — 29 May
Schemes as functors from commutative rings to sets.
Rings: commutative with unit; homomorphisms preserve $1$. $K$ a ring (fixed ground ring).
$P_I = K[T_i]_{i\in I}$ (any set $I$); affine space $K^I=\{x=(x_i)\}$.
f\in P_I\ \longmapsto\ \tilde f\colon K^I\to K,\quad x\mapsto f(x)
$P_I$ is the $K$-algebra generated by the $T_i$: for a $K$-algebra $K'$
\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(P_I,K')\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ K'^{\,I},\qquad u\mapsto (u(T_i))_{i\in I}
x\in K^I\ \leftrightarrow\ \varepsilon_x\colon P_I\to K,\qquad f(x)=\varepsilon_x(f)
(f+g)(x)=f(x)+g(x),\quad (fg)(x)=f(x)g(x),\quad (\lambda f)(x)=\lambda f(x)
Equations: $f_j\in P_I$, $j\in J$; $\;f_j(x)=0$.
Let $x$ vary in $K'^I$, $K'$ an arbitrary $K$-algebra.
Standard affine algebraic space
E^I\colon K'\mapsto K'^I,\qquad u\colon K'\to K''\ \mapsto\ u^I\colon K'^I\to K''^I
V_S(K')=\{x\in K'^I : f_j(x)=0\ \ \forall j\}\ \subset E^I(K')
$V_S$ is a subfunctor of $E^I$ (in the category of functors from $K$-algebras to sets).
Two studies of $V_S$: (1) intrinsic, up to isomorphism of functors; (2) the embedding $V_S\subset E^I$.
f=\sum_j g_j f_j\ (g_j\in P_I)\ \Longrightarrow\ f(x)=\sum_j g_j(x)f_j(x)=0
$J\subset P_I$ the ideal generated by the $f_j$: the equations $f_j(x)=0$ are equivalent to $f(x)=0$ for all $f\in J$.
Subfunctors of $E^I$ defined by equations $\leftrightarrow$ ideals $J\subset P_I$.
Claim
The functors isomorphic to some $V_S$ are exactly the representable functors
h_A\colon K'\mapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-alg}}(A,K'),\qquad A\in \mathcal C_K
$h_A$ embeds in $E^I$ as a $V_S$ iff $A\simeq P_I/J$, i.e. $A$ is generated by a family $(a_i)_{i\in I}$.
An isomorphism $V_A\simeq V_S\subset E^I$ is the same as a family of generators of $A$ indexed by $I$.
